items.excerpt: Israel presses ahead with West Bank operation as election approaches TEL AVIV, Israel (AP) — The Israeli military is pressing ahead with a massive operation in the occupied West Bank that has displaced hundreds of Palestinians. The move follows a gun attack in Hebron on Friday that killed two Israeli soldiers and wounded three others. As Israel approaches a tense election, the military has placed major restrictions on Palestinian movement. On Sunday, they announced that most Palestinian workers with permits would not be allowed into Israeli settlements for work. The military claims to have operated in over 400 locations over the weekend, arresting 40 Palestinians linked to Hamas or Palestinian Islamic Jihad. Brazil votes in a tense Lula vs Bolsonaro runoff with US influence over Latin America at stake RIO DE JANEIRO (AP) — Brazilians are choosing between President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Flávio Bolsonaro in a polarizing presidential election. The vote will determine if the U.S. expands its influence in the region. Polls show a close race. Lula is a left-of-center veteran facing Bolsonaro, who is an ally of President Donald Trump and the son of former President Jair Bolsonaro. Flávio Bolsonaro led in the first round. Both candidates have faced corruption allegations. Lula portrays Bolsonaro as a threat to democracy while Bolsonaro promises economic reforms. The election reflects Brazil's divided political landscape with significant implications for U.S.-Brazil relations. More than 400,000 protest across France, challenging Macron as Paris clashes erupt PARIS (AP) — Clashes erupted in Paris as a mass march drew to a close Saturday. More than 400,000 people rallied across France over school funding and soaring living costs, challenging President Emmanuel Macron. Police made nearly 1,000 arrests. The Paris march began peacefully but turned violent near its endpoint. Masked protesters hurled objects and fireworks at police, who responded with tear gas and water cannons. The Interior Ministry reported 410,000 protesters nationwide, while the CGT union estimated nearly 800,000. This unrest is testing Macron's authority in the final months of his presidency before elections in May. Ukraine and Russia eye new peace talks — and Melania Trump's mission — but steep obstacles remain KYIV, Ukraine (AP) — Ukraine and Russia have signaled willingness to resume peace talks and back a humanitarian mission led by U.S. First lady Melania Trump, but deep disagreements over territory and security guarantees underscore obstacles to ending the war. U.S. President Donald Trump is pushing for a new round of negotiations, potentially in mid-November, as Russia continues to demand control of Ukrainian regions it illegally annexed but does not fully control. Kyiv rejects any suggestion of unilateral withdrawal and says stronger Western pressure on Moscow is needed to advance peace efforts. Trump casts his midterm ballot early in Florida WEST PALM BEACH, Fla. (AP) — President Donald Trump has cast his ballot in the midterm elections, voting for all Republicans in Florida before speaking at a Georgia rally. Trump and first lady Melania Trump arrived at their West Palm Beach polling location together Saturday after Trump spent the morning at his nearby golf course. Trump has endorsed Republican Rep. Byron Donalds, who is running against David Jolly, a Republican-turned-independent-turned-Democrat, to succeed term-limited Gov. Ron DeSantis. He has also campaigned for Republican Sen. Ashley Moody, who is running to fill the last two years of Secretary of State Marco Rubio’s former Senate term against progressive state lawmaker Angie Nixon. Saudi Arabia reopens airport as attacks by Houthi rebels persist, and other Mideast news Saudi Arabia has reopened its main airport for international flights after strikes by Yemen's Houthi rebels knocked it out of service. On Sunday, the kingdom intercepted and destroyed a missile and drone fired by the Houthis. Meanwhile, Israel is conducting a military operation in the West Bank following an attack that killed two Israeli soldiers. This comes just days before Israel’s election, seen as a referendum on Prime Minister Netanyahu’s leadership. In other news, Iran’s foreign minister dismissed threats of war, and a Libyan leader rejected comments by U.S. President Donald Trump labeling Libya as "terror-infested." Musk says he was behind Starlink speed restriction after service in Ukraine is restored KYIV, Ukraine (AP) — Ukraine's access to Starlink and Starshield satellite links has been restored to previous speeds, according to President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. He announced Saturday that the restoration began overnight, improving front-line logistics and defense against Russian drones. It comes as U.S. envoys have pushed for an end to the war. Russia agreed Wednesday to resume negotiations with Washington and Kyiv next month. A localized ceasefire was also brokered Friday by first lady Melania Trump in Ukraine's Kherson region. The limitations on Starshield had alarmed Ukraine's military, adding to tensions between Kyiv and Washington. Meanwhile, missile attacks and power blackouts continue in the region. ... Soldiers guard center of Milan as thousands of protesters march in cities across Europe MILAN (AP) — Thousands of young people marched through Italian cities like Milan, Rome, and Turin on Saturday. Authorities deployed soldiers in Milan, where previous protests turned violent, but the demonstrations remained peaceful. There were brief clashes with police in Rome and Turin. Italian Premier Giorgia Meloni has announced measures, including tougher penalties for minors involved in protests. Demonstrations also occurred in other European cities, addressing issues like education, corruption, and housing. In Albania, protests turned violent, while in Spain and Portugal, demonstrators focused on pensions and housing concerns. New York's archdiocese and survivors of clergy abuse agree to $800 million legal settlement The Archdiocese of New York and attorneys for about 1,300 parishioners who say they were sexually abused by clergy have agreed to an $800 million settlement of their legal claims. It is the second-largest involving a Catholic archdiocese in the U.S., following a 2024 settlement of $880 million involving the Archdiocese of Los Angeles. New York Archbishop Ronald Hicks sent an email Saturday to clergy confirming the settlement after attorneys for the survivors of alleged abuse announced it. Abuse survivor attorney Jeff Anderson said the settlement represents a powerful moment in the pursuit of justice. Hicks said in his email that the settlement will bring healing and reconciliation. Serbia holds a parliamentary election as strongman Vucic faces protesting students BELGRADE, Serbia (AP) — Serbians are voting in a parliamentary election seen as a showdown between strongman leader Aleksandar Vucic and a student-led movement. The election is shaping up as a referendum between Vucic's right-wing party and the Students' List. The main contenders are polling neck-and-neck, making it the most uncertain election in recent years. The European Union is closely watching the vote due to past irregularities. If his party wins, Vucic plans to return as prime minister. The Students' List, a new movement, aims to counter Vucic's rule with a non-partisan approach. The outcome remains uncertain, with fears of postelection instability.

items.title: Fed expected to hold rates steady this week despite hot inflation — but signal they're not done hiking
items.excerpt: The Federal Reserve heads into its interest-rate decision this week facing hotter inflation, keeping the meeting live even as markets widely expect the central bank to hold interest rates steady just days before the midterm elections. ... "This is a perfect time for clear forward guidance that doesn't quite say, but strongly hints, we're pausing now, but we stand ready to raise again and even give a hint that the next meeting might be the next interest rate hike." Inflation heated up in September, as the Consumer Price Index accelerated to 3.7% from a year earlier. Core CPI, which excludes food and energy, ticked up to 2.6%, while wholesale prices jumped more than 6%, and the Fed's preferred inflation gauge — the core Personal Consumption Expenditures index — is projected to top 3%. ... In his last remarks before this week's policy meeting, many observers think Warsh underscored what Fed Vice Chair Philip Jefferson and New York Fed president John Williams previously said: that despite hot inflation reports, they would like to take time to review the data as they consider the prospect of further rate hikes. Warsh neither endorsed nor pushed back on his colleagues' recent signals that they'd like to wait for more data, but he noted that the world had "broadly conformed to our expectations" since the Fed's September meeting. ... After raising rates for the first time in more than three years in September, minutes from that meeting read that most participants assessed that another increase would likely be appropriate by year-end. ... The Fed's benchmark rate is currently in the range of 3.75% to 4%. Traders are pricing in nearly 90% odds it will hold next week, but see 70% odds of a quarter-point hike in December.

items.title: US Business Activity Keeps Fed Inflation Pressure High
items.excerpt: WASHINGTON — U.S. business activity remained firmly in expansion territory in October even as growth cooled slightly from September, while companies raised selling prices at the fastest pace in more than four years. The combination of strong demand and persistent pricing power gives the Federal Reserve another reason to remain cautious as policymakers prepare for their Oct. 27-28 meeting. ... The latest US business activity data show an economy that is still growing quickly enough to generate inflation pressure. S&P Global’s flash Composite PMI slipped to 57.6 from 58.4 in September, while its output-price index climbed to 59.8, the highest reading since August 2022. ... The inflation signal in the survey is more concerning than the slight cooling in headline activity. Businesses across both manufacturing and services reported raising output prices more aggressively, suggesting that higher input costs are being passed through to customers rather than absorbed entirely in profit margins. The output-price index rose to 59.8 from 58.4 in September. Input costs eased slightly to 64.9 from 65.9, but they remain historically elevated, especially for manufacturers exposed to energy, transportation and imported materials. ... American News Brief reported that consumer inflation accelerated to 3.7% in September as gasoline prices and other costs increased. The October PMI now suggests that businesses may be adding another layer of price pressure by passing more of their own expenses through to buyers. ... Energy-market disruptions linked to the Iran conflict remain an important source of pressure. Higher fuel and freight costs can spread from transportation into manufacturing, wholesale distribution and services, increasing the risk that an external oil shock becomes embedded in broader inflation. ... ## Fed Is Expected to Hold Rates Steady Next Week ... Despite the inflation warning, most economists do not expect the Federal Reserve to raise rates at its October meeting. A Reuters poll found that 94 of 100 economists expect the Fed to keep the federal funds target at 3.75% to 4.00% on Oct. 27-28, while all respondents expected another increase in December. ... The survey may be more important for December than for next week’s decision. If the Fed pauses in October, another month of elevated inflation, ... For consumers, the concern is that inflation pressure is migrating beyond gasoline and other directly visible energy costs. If service providers and manufacturers continue raising prices because demand remains strong, households could face another period in which wage gains struggle to keep up with everyday expenses. ... US business activity therefore presents the Fed with an uncomfortable combination heading into next week’s meeting. The economy remains resilient enough to grow, but that same resilience is helping companies raise prices, increasing the chance that inflation stays above target and that monetary policy remains tight well into 2027.

items.title: Obama campaigns for Democrats, and France demonstrations continue: Weekend Rundown
items.excerpt: Former President Barack Obama, appearing in Ohio on Saturday at his first campaign rally of this fall’s midterm elections, called President Donald Trump an agent of “chaos and cruelty” and a man of broken promises. Obama’s visit was aimed at boosting two Democrats: Amy Acton, the party’s nominee for governor; and former Sen. Sherrod Brown, who has mounted a comeback bid for his old job. Obama was particularly scornful of Vivek Ramaswamy’s attack ad aimed at Acton, saying there is “no line” Ramaswamy won’t cross. Later in the night, Obama rallied for Michigan’s Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed in Detroit. The city, where 75% of the population is Black, is crucial to statewide victories. ... ## Iranian plots to kill U.S. officials have reached ‘advanced stages,’ intel memo warns ... Iran has stepped up efforts to target U.S. personnel in the Middle East and elsewhere, according to a memo Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton sent to Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Friday. The memo warned that “the lethal plotting efforts by the Iranians against U.S. citizens have reached advanced stages.” A U.S. official confirmed the memo’s authenticity to NBC News after it was first reported by Axios. The intelligence comes days after sources told NBC News that the U.S. military has been quietly scaling back its troop presence at bases across the Middle East. The State Department has also ordered further staff reductions at multiple diplomatic posts in the region, including in Lebanon, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar and Jordan, according to a State Department official. ... ## Mass protests challenge Macron as French police use tear gas and water cannons More than 100,000 people marched in Paris on Saturday over school funding and soaring living costs, challenging President Emmanuel Macron’s government in a largely peaceful demonstration before clashes broke out near the march’s end point. Students, union members, environmentalists and other groups marched through cold, rainy weather. Near the march’s end point, some demonstrators threw bottles and rocks at police, who then charged at the crowd, fired tear gas and used water cannons. NBC News witnessed no looting.

items.title: Trump's Election Attacks Enter New Pre-emptive Phase
items.excerpt: For months, President Trump has mounted a sustained effort to attack the integrity of U.S. elections while using the federal government to try to assert more control over the voting process overseen by states. Last week, Mr. Trump opened a new front. Rather than simply push false claims at his rallies or target voters his administration claims should not be on the rolls, Mr. Trump moved to pre-emptively challenge the certification of Alaska’s Senate election if the Republican candidate narrowly loses. In doing so, Mr. Trump harnessed the power of the federal government to try to interfere in the voting process before Election Day — essentially trying to nullify an opponent’s potential win before the game has been called. items.excerpt: Before we got there, Quentin Tarantino surprised an AFI Fest crowd with the first 17 minutes of The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth, providing the first extended look at David Fincher’s continuation of Once Upon a Time in Hollywood. DC Studios also appears to have another theatrical win with Clayface, Paramount+ moved another step closer to being folded into HBO Max’s creative structure, and Charli xcx added Martin Scorsese to an increasingly ridiculous list of filmmakers she has worked with. ... Brad Pitt returns as Cliff Booth in a story set in 1977, eight years after the events of Once Upon a Time in Hollywood. Tarantino wrote the screenplay while David Fincher directs, creating one of the stranger filmmaker combinations in recent memory. The new movie positions Cliff as a Hollywood fixer who spends part of his time working at the New Beverly Cinema while dealing with situations requiring the kind of morally flexible problem-solving that made him so memorable the first time around.

Why big music stars like Harry Styles and Celine Dion are embracing residencies NEW YORK (AP) — Harry Styles' residency at Madison Square Garden has drawn tens of thousands of fans eager for an exclusive experience. His run is the latest in a trend. Residencies are growing among pop stars, with artists like Bad Bunny, Usher and Carín León embracing the style of performance. Residency pioneer Celine Dion has also returned to the format. Industry insiders say residencies offer benefits like reduced travel stress and elaborate stage productions. However, some fans argue that costs are shifted to them, with high ticket prices and travel expenses to see the shows. While residencies provide artists a break from touring, experts emphasize the importance of traditional tours to reach fans who can't travel. ... Tom Skerritt, Emmy-winning actor with roles in 'Picket Fences,' 'Alien' and 'Top Gun,' dies at 93 NEW YORK (AP) — An Emmy-winning actor known for roles in “Top Gun” and “Picket Fences,” Tom Skerritt has died at 93. His family said in a statement he died Wednesday of natural causes. Skerritt won an Emmy for “Picket Fences” in 1993 and was known for roles in “Turning Point,” “Steel Magnolias,” and “Contact.” He was once described as a character actor in a leading man’s body. Skerritt also performed onstage, including in “Our Town” and “A Time to Kill.” His family highlighted his passion for storytelling and helping others.
